tagline: Four wars, three warning signals, one exposed neighbour: open data can tell India where to look next month.
ai_declaration: AI tools declaration: the team used Anthropic's Claude (an AI assistant) to help write and debug code, draft text and design visuals. All analysis choices, numbers and conclusions were checked by the team, and every number is generated by the pipeline from the official competition data.

gdelt.caveat: GDELT counts media-coded reports, not incidents; it is a narrative/attention signal and is compared with UCDP, never joined on events. These are new results, not part of the submitted models.

india.note: D10 keeps the deadlier records outside the focus countries, so India figures are a floor.

prereg.rule: Primary metric: mean PR-AUC over the 2023-2025 back-test folds (escalation is rare, ~2% of area-months). Adopt a variant over the current case-only model only if its mean PR-AUC is at least 5% higher AND its mean ROC-AUC is not lower. Among qualifying variants take the highest PR-AUC. 2026 is scored once, after this file is written, and the choice is not changed afterwards.

limits: 92% of 2026 RU–UA deaths have no sub-national location.

Decisions to start wars are not forecastable from death counts.
